chunks.text: Can you read this?
Did you understand it right away?
Only one question matters here: do I get my money back, or not?
If you hesitated, you are not alone.
844,000 adults in Switzerland struggle with reading.
Letters like this decide their money, their deadlines, their rights.
No one should be shut out of them.
But easy-language versions are slow expert work, and a chatbot checks nothing.
Leicht·Facile drafts easy-language versions of official texts with Apertus, the Swiss open model.
It does not replace the writers.
It gives them a checked first draft.
Apertus does what needs language understanding.
Plain code checks everything that can be counted.
Apertus turns a letter into a fact sheet: every deadline, amount and phone number.
Then it writes a draft.
Every sentence links back to its source; every omission is explained.
Code checks 42 Swiss easy-language rules, and every date and amount.
A larger Apertus model judges the meaning.
Only flagged sentences are repaired.
The writer approves every block, with a full audit trail.
The same sentence, now.
Short. Clear. The answer comes first.
Against a strong single prompt: less than a third of the rule errors.
And no fact goes missing unnoticed.
Patient letters, child protection decisions, tax letters:
under secrecy, they may not go to a foreign cloud.
Closed models stay with their makers.
Most open models keep their training data closed.
Most fully open ones are built abroad.
Apertus is open down to its data, built and trained in Switzerland, and runs in-house.
Ticino already runs it for sensitive documents.
For these letters, it is the only option.
